blocks.text: Where it sits and what to know here

items.t: Chilliwack Mountain is a residential hillside neighbourhood in the City of Chilliwack, on the named mountain on the south side of the Fraser River, just west of Chilliwack Creek and west of the downtown core. The City treats Chilliwack Mountain as a neighbourhood in its own reporting but does not publish a street-by-street boundary for the board sub-area name.

The community sits above the Industrial Way / Progress Way industrial area on the valley floor; the City's Schweyey Road forcemain page places the mountain community above that industrial area, with sewage service along Schweyey Road for Chilliwack Mountain and portions of Industrial Way and Progress Way. The residential streets are the mountain roads themselves — Chilliwack Mountain Road, Grandview Drive and Hillkeep Place at the top, and Sunrise Drive on the slopes.

Where attached stock concentrates — townhouses only: the Chilliwack Mountain Road corridor, where the townhouse complexes stand at 43610–43680 and 43998 Chilliwack Mountain Road, and Sunrise Drive, where Maple Hills stands at 8590 Sunrise Drive.

The mountain is a detached-hillside market by zoning: the City's hillside zones set HR (Hillside Residential) lots at a minimum of 0.2 ha on community water and 0.4 ha otherwise, RH (Rural Hillside) at 8 ha, SHR (Suburban Hillside Residential) by a slope table from 360 m² to 990 m², and SR (Suburban Residential) at 650 m² on full services — lot forms that produce houses, not apartment buildings.

The mountain has no neighbourhood plan: Schedule B of the Chilliwack 2050 OCP contains no Chilliwack Mountain neighbourhood plan (Schedules B1–B7 cover other areas); the mountain's future form is governed by the hillside Development Permit Areas D-2 and D-5, not by a densification plan — a structural reason not to expect apartment product to be planned onto the mountain under the current OCP.

Two townhouse clusters sit almost side by side on Chilliwack Mountain Road and are easy to conflate: the DP000817 complex at 43660/43710 (applicant Cedarsky Developments Ltd., in 2017 council records) and Reflections @ Cedar Sky at 43680.

Osprey Ridge's "year built" changes by listing — 2022 in the building summary, 2023 and 2026 on individual units — because the 34-home development was phased. Warranty and depreciation-report timing follow the phase your unit sits in, not the complex name.

Hillkeep Regional Park is the mountain's amenity anchor: an FVRD nature reserve at the top of the mountain on Hillkeep Place, reached by Grandview Drive, with hiking trails and a viewing platform — the documented recreation draw for every complex on the mountain, in place of any in-complex amenity building (none of the complexes is published with one).

Chilliwack's late-payment penalties are a dated, published fact a new owner should know: City of Chilliwack property taxes for 2026 were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty after July 2, 2026 and an additional 5% after August 4, 2026, and drainage and dyking taxes are levied on top of the municipal rate.

The nearest full services are off the mountain: Chilliwack Landing Leisure Centre at 9145 Corbould Street, Chilliwack Library at 45860 First Avenue, and Chilliwack General Hospital at 45600 Menholm Road are all on the valley floor — the mountain itself has no known grocery store, leisure centre or library branch.

blocks.text: Where it sits and what to know here

items.t: Where the townhouse stock concentrates: the Chilliwack Mountain Road corridor — Reflections @ Cedar Sky and Eagles Perch at the 43610–43680 stretch, Westpointe at 43777, Osprey Ridge at 43998 — and Sunrise Drive, where Maple Hills stands at 8590 Sunrise Drive.

Nearby areas: Chilliwack Downtown and Chilliwack Proper West to the east, Little Mountain to the southeast, Fairfield Island across the river to the north, and the Lickman Road / Industrial Way corridor below the mountain to the west.
Chilliwack is CADREB ground, not Fraser Valley Real Estate Board (FVREB) territory.

Transit: no BC Transit route runs onto the mountain's residential streets; the closest listed service is route 59 Industrial – Downtown Chilliwack via the Lickman Park & Ride, with peak-period trips, and Highway 1 access is via the Lickman Road interchange south of the mountain.

Strata vs fee-simple — the core distinction: four of the five counted complexes are confirmed strata. A strata townhouse buyer owns a strata lot, pays strata fees, and gets a Form B package. A fee-simple townhouse buyer owns the lot outright: no strata, no Form B, no strata fees — municipal rules and any registered covenants/HOA only.
Services: the City states the Schweyey Road forcemain provides sewage services for Chilliwack Mountain and portions of Industrial Way and Progress Way.

Lot size on the mountain is slope-driven, not just area-driven: in the SHR zone the minimum lot area rises from 360 m² in the lowest slope band to 990 m² in the highest — a lot's subdivision or rebuild potential depends on its measured slope.

There is no neighbourhood plan coming to change this: no Chilliwack Mountain plan appears in Schedule B (B1 to B7) of the Chilliwack 2050 OCP — the mountain is governed by the city-wide OCP and its hillside Development Permit Areas D-2 and D-5.

The park at the top is regional, not municipal: Hillkeep Regional Park (FVRD) is a nature reserve at the top of Chilliwack Mountain on Hillkeep Place, reached by Grandview Drive, with hiking trails and a viewing platform — the documented draw the mountainside complexes market against.

The nearest services are all off the mountain: Chilliwack Landing Leisure Centre (9145 Corbould St), Chilliwack Library (45860 First Avenue), Chilliwack General Hospital (45600 Menholm Rd) and the Chilliwack Urgent and Primary Care Centre (#104 – 7955 Evans Road) — mountain households are car-dependent by design, with no bus route on the residential streets.
Drainage and dyking taxes ride on top of the municipal rate in Chilliwack — a small line on the tax notice that valley-floor systems explain, and one a mountain buyer still pays.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Chilliwack Mountain

items.t: Confirmed housing/land form: hillside residential lots carrying single-detached houses, with the housing form governed by the City's hillside development permit areas D-2 and D-5. Fee-simple is the default form: own title, no strata, no Form B, no strata fees.

Lot character from the hillside zones, as the bylaw states it: HR (Hillside Residential) Zone, minimum lot area 0.2 ha where served by a community water system and 0.4 ha for all other uses, minimum lot width 25 m; RH (Rural Hillside) Zone, minimum lot area 8 ha and minimum lot width 25 m; SHR (Suburban Hillside Residential) Zone, minimum lot area set by the zone's slope table, starting at 360 m² for the lowest slope band and rising to 990 m² for the highest; SR (Suburban Residential) Zone, minimum lot area 650 m² where served by community water and community sanitary sewer, minimum lot width 17.5 m on the same services — all under City of Chilliwack Zoning Bylaw No. 5000. These are zone minimums, not a claim that every mountain lot is that size.

Slope is the lot character: in the SHR zone the minimum lot area rises with slope band (360 m² → 990 m²), so a lot's subdivision or rebuild potential depends on its measured slope, not just its area. Price buildable, permit-able area — not gross area and not view alone.
Tenure caution — Westpointe (43777 Chilliwack Mountain Road)

blocks.text: Where it sits and what to know here

items.t: Residential streets are the mountain roads themselves — Chilliwack Mountain Road, Grandview Drive and Hillkeep Place at the top, and Sunrise Drive on the slopes. Highway 1 access is via the Lickman Road interchange south of the mountain, where BC Transit's Lickman Park & Ride sits.

Transit: no BC Transit route in the Chilliwack route list runs onto Chilliwack Mountain residential streets; the closest listed service is route 59 Industrial – Downtown Chilliwack to Cottonwood Mall via the Lickman Park & Ride, with peak-period trips.
Schools: no SD33 public school is located on Chilliwack Mountain itself; the schools physically in Chilliwack listed in the provincial school directory are all on the valley floor or in Sardis.

Hillside permit rule — the governing lot rule on the mountain: Development Permit Area D-2 applies to Chilliwack Mountain, and a permit with a geotechnical hazard and slope assessment is required before subdivision, construction, land clearing or earthworks. Budget the report and permit timing into any build, subdivision or renovation plan. DPA D-5 (Hillside Development) also covers the mountain.

Hillkeep Regional Park (FVRD) is the top-of-mountain anchor: a nature reserve at the top of Chilliwack Mountain on Hillkeep Place, reached by Grandview Drive via Hillkeep Place, with hiking trails and a viewing platform — open-space/park ground that shapes the mountain's top, not buildable lot area.

Everything else is down the hill: no City leisure centre, library branch, shopping centre or grocery store on the mountain is known — the nearest leisure centre is Chilliwack Landing Leisure Centre, 9145 Corbould St; the nearest library is Chilliwack Library, 45860 First Avenue; the nearest grocery named in City material is Save-on-Foods Sardis, 6014 Vedder Road, in Sardis; Chilliwack General Hospital is at 45600 Menholm Rd, and the Chilliwack Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at #104 – 7955 Evans Road. Mountain land is bought for slope, view and trails, at the price of a drive for everything else.

Households here are car-dependent by design: no bus route serves the mountain's residential streets and the closest service is route 59 at the Lickman Park & Ride — factor access into lot value, especially on the upper roads in winter conditions.

blocks.text: Acreage and rural land in Chilliwack Mountain

What acreage trades on Chilliwack Mountain: large fee-simple hillside parcels — single-detached lots whose size is set by the hillside zones, from SHR slope-band lots (360 m² to 990 m²) and SR lots (650 m² on full services) up through HR lots at 0.2 ha (community water) / 0.4 ha (all other uses) and RH (Rural Hillside) ground at an 8 ha minimum. The hectare-scale HR/RH parcels are the mountain's real acreage form.

items.t: Seasons at Cedar Sky: a master-planned townhome community on the north face of the mountain, marketed from 2015 newspaper advertisements (show home at 43685 Chilliwack Mountain Rd) and described in a neighbourhood source as built 2014, sitting immediately beside the Reflections @ Cedar Sky addresses.

blocks.text: Where it sits and what to know here

items.t: Municipality: City of Chilliwack, BC. Chilliwack Mountain is a residential hillside neighbourhood on the named mountain on the south side of the Fraser River, just west of Chilliwack Creek and west of the downtown core. No separate official alternate name was confirmed.

Recreation / library: there is no City leisure centre on the mountain; the nearest is Chilliwack Landing Leisure Centre, 9145 Corbould St. There is no Fraser Valley Regional Library branch on the mountain; the nearest is Chilliwack Library, 45860 First Avenue.
Chilliwack General Hospital, 45600 Menholm Rd, provides emergency care (Fraser Health), and the Chilliwack Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at #104 – 7955 Evans Road.

Slope and hazard rules: Development Permit Area D-2 applies to Chilliwack Mountain, and a permit with a geotechnical hazard and slope assessment is required before subdivision, construction, land clearing or earthworks. Budget for the hillside permit process: the report and permit timing belong in any build, subdivision or renovation plan for a mountain parcel.

The mountain has no neighbourhood plan: No Chilliwack Mountain neighbourhood plan appears in Schedule B of the Chilliwack 2050 OCP (Bylaw 5500, Schedules B1 to B7); the mountain is governed by Schedule D Development Permit Areas D-2 Hillside Environment and D-5 Hillside Development. A land pitch citing a "Chilliwack Mountain neighbourhood plan" is citing a document the OCP does not contain.

Westpointe's own sources disagree on its build year: A current listing describes a Westpointe home as built 2003; a neighbourhood source describes the complex as built 2004 with 34 rancher townhome units.

faq.q: Is there any apartment condo on Chilliwack Mountain?

faq.q: Is there an age restriction at the mountain townhouses?

faq.a: For a long-term tenancy, a rental-restriction bylaw cannot stop you — those bylaws have been void since November 24, 2022 anywhere in BC. Short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw.

faq.a: DPA D-2 covers the mountain: a development permit with a geotechnical hazard and slope assessment is required before subdivision, construction, land clearing or earthworks. For a strata, that regime sits behind major exterior or common-property projects, not day-to-day ownership — but it is a real cost and timing factor in a complex's long-range planning, and it is one more thing the depreciation report should reflect.

faq.a: If it is a bylaw, only a 55+ threshold is lawful in BC (SPA ss. 123.1/123.2). Read the bylaws before marketing or buying on that basis.

That directory line reflects a rental-restriction bylaw, and rental-restriction bylaws are void since November 24, 2022 — long-term rentals cannot be banned by bylaw, though short-term rentals can still be restricted. Confirm the current registered bylaws on the Form B.

faq.a: A large fee-simple hillside parcel — most distinctively an HR lot (0.2 ha minimum on community water, 0.4 ha otherwise) or RH ground (8 ha minimum) — carrying or intended for a single-detached house, governed by the D-2 / D-5 hillside permit areas. There is no acreage subdivision, no bare-land strata and no presale acreage product to buy instead.
